licenses.issuingAuthority: Uttarakhand Pollution Control Board (UKPCB) - Regional Office for Green/Orange category applications under Rs 5 crore investment; Head Office (Member Secretary level) for Red category or higher-investment applications

portal.name: Invest Uttarakhand Single Window System (with redirection to the OCMMS portal after in-principle CAF approval)

timeline.basis: Statutory application timeline varies by risk category per the ED's 'Application Timeline' table: Green 30 days, Orange 45 days, Red 45 days. A separate minimum 15-day window applies to the earlier in-principle Common Application Form (CAF) approval stage.
timeline.text: CTE applications are processed in 30 days for Green category and 45 days for Orange and Red categories, after an earlier in-principle CAF approval stage that takes a minimum of 15 days.

documents: DIC/SIA/Mining Lease/Conceptual Plan (in case of Building/Infrastructure project) etc.
Land allotment letter/land allotment LOI/Land Conversion Certificate for industrial uses
Layout plan of the project/industry site
Project report including complete details of raw materials (per month), production capacity (per month) and proposed investment
Manufacturing process along with detailed process flow chart
Article of Association / Memorandum of Understanding
Proposal for waste water treatment & disposal along with details of water consumption, waste water generation & installed capacity of treatment system (KLD)
Proposal for Air Pollution Control measures along with fuel types and daily consumption
Hazardous Waste/E-Waste etc. Management Plan
Permission of CGWA (if applicable)

deemedApproval.text: Deemed approval mechanisms exist within the automated online system if the department fails to respond or process the file within stipulated statutory timelines without raising queries; auto-renewal is enabled primarily for Green category industries operating on a self-declaration basis.

validity.text: Validity is 10 years for Green category and 5 years for Orange and Red categories.

fees.text: Initial CTE fees are calculated based on the net/gross capital investment of the unit and its risk category, with a baseline fee rate of Rs 10,000; application fees cover initial scrutiny and physical inspection expenses.

steps.title: Register on Single Window System portal
steps.note: Applicant registers on the Invest Uttarakhand Single Window System using Aadhaar and PAN.

steps.title: Submit Common Application Form (CAF) for in-principle approval
steps.note: For a fresh unit, the CAF routes the application across relevant departments (e.g., Tourism, Fire, Pollution Control Board).

steps.title: Redirect to OCMMS portal after in-principle approval
steps.note: Occurs automatically once in-principle CAF approval is obtained (minimum 15 days).

steps.title: Fill technical form and pay fee
steps.note: Applicant fills details on Air, Water and other parameters and pays fees based on investment and industry classification.

steps.title: File routed to Regional Office (RO)
steps.note: Once submitted and fees settled, the file is routed to the concerning RO login.

steps.title: Plan/map approval to proceed with construction
steps.note: Upon satisfactory technical scrutiny, the plan/map is approved, allowing construction per approved plans.

steps.title: AEE scrutiny of file
steps.note: Assistant Environment Engineer verifies categorization, investment figures, and Air/Water/ETP/STP/hazardous waste plans.

steps.title: Query/revert or field inspection
steps.note: If shortcomings are found, a query is raised or the file reverted; if complete, a field inspection is conducted for units outside industrial areas.

steps.title: Final approval
steps.note: Granted at RO level for Green/Orange under Rs 5 crore investment, or forwarded to Head Office for Member Secretary-level approval for Red category or higher investment.

remarks: Field officers handle 2 to 3 districts per regional office.
4 plain districts (Haridwar, Udham Singh Nagar, Dehradun, Kotdwar plain belts) handle major industrial/pharma units, while the 9 hilly districts handle hotel and tourism sectors.
Multi-year validity reduced annual application loops from approximately 8,000 repeating cases per year down to 5-10% fresh applications.

findings.text: Officials note data fragmentation across government systems - SIDCUL, Registry Department, Development Authorities (e.g., MDDA) and SPCB are not fully unified for private land.
Small and micro enterprises are heavily dependent on third-party consultants due to low awareness of regulatory renewal/filing timelines.
In-principle CAF approval carries only a stated minimum timeline of 15 days before the application is redirected to the OCMMS portal.

Implementation of multi-year consent validities (5-10 years) was cited as eliminating yearly application friction, cutting repeat annual applications from about 8,000/year to 5-10% fresh applications.
The department is migrating towards UCAMS, CPCB's centralized Unified Consent Management System.

Common scrutiny rejections include incorrect industry risk categorization, misalignment or underreporting of declared gross investment, defective or unapproved land documentation (e.g., missing Section 143 conversion, unpassed MDDA maps), inadequate ETP/STP capacity, and absence of valid hazardous-waste disposal agreements.
Officials recommend integrating land records, SIDCUL, development authority (MDDA), and revenue registry databases directly into the Single Window System to auto-fetch land data.
Officials recommend developing region-specific environmental policies tailored to geographical realities (e.g., hilly-terrain STP effluent management) rather than uniform nationwide templates.
Officials suggest cost-effective or shared monitoring solutions for MSMEs to reduce the financial burden of individual Rs 15-20 lakh RTMS installations.
Officials recommend simplifying compliance reporting workflows to reduce small units' dependency on external consultants.
Field officers handle 2 to 3 districts per regional office.
4 plain districts handle major industrial/pharma units while the 9 hilly districts primarily handle hotel and tourism sector applications.
A deemed-approval mechanism and auto-renewal facility for Green category industries (self-declaration basis) are built into the automated online system.
CTE fees carry a baseline rate of Rs 10,000 and are otherwise calculated from net/gross capital investment and risk category.
Processing timelines differ by risk category: 30 days for Green, 45 days for Orange and Red.

gaps.text: The in-principle CAF approval stage is described only with a minimum timeline of 15 days; no maximum or typical duration is given.

In the narrative 'Application Process Flow', Step 6 describes the plan/map being approved before Step 7 describes the AEE's scrutiny process that would lead to that approval - the two steps appear out of logical order in the source document.
The document does not state whether the applicant must visit any physical UKPCB office at any stage; only the officer-conducted site inspection is described.
Multi-year consent validity is credited with cutting repeat annual CTE applications from about 8,000/year to 5-10% fresh applications - a concrete, quantified improvement.
The 'Best Practices' section for CTE is left blank ('-') in the source document, meaning no specific best practice was recorded for this service.
Statutory fee is given only as a 'baseline' of Rs 10,000; the actual slab/formula tying fee amount to investment size and risk category is referenced but not detailed.
Migration toward UCAMS (CPCB's centralized Unified Consent Management System) is mentioned as underway, but no timeline or completion status is given.

NOCs from Departments (as applicable)

steps.title: Register on Single Window System portal
steps.note: Applicant registers on the Invest Uttarakhand Single Window System using Aadhaar and PAN.

steps.title: Fill online application and upload documents
steps.note: Includes details demonstrating compliance with applicable CTE conditions.

steps.title: PCB User ID created and redirected to OCMMS CCA dashboard
steps.note: SMS/e-mail intimation is also provided.

steps.title: Complete technical details and pay consent fee
steps.note: Fee calculated via an online fee calculator; documents uploaded and fee paid online.

steps.title: Site inspection

steps.title: CCA/CTO approved and issued

remarks: Field officers handle 2 to 3 districts per regional office.
CTO inspections verify output discharge parameter compliance (BOD, COD, stack emissions) and equipment adequacy, rather than just physical structure.

The document's header lists the service discussed as 'Consent to Establish,' though the content throughout describes the Consent to Operate (CCA/CTO) process - likely a labeling carry-over from the companion CTE record (same date, location, and experts).

findings.text: The ED document's header metadata lists 'Consent to Establish' as the service discussed, but the process, terminology (CCA/CTO, OCMMS CCA dashboard, CTO baseline fee) and documentation described are for Consent to Operate, indicating a likely labeling error in the source document.
High financial burden of continuous monitoring equipment (OCMS/RTMS costing Rs 15-20 lakh) falls on MSME units.
Small units depend on external consultants due to lack of internal EHS teams and low awareness of annual compliance schedules.
Terrain-specific operational challenges exist in hilly districts, e.g., treated STP effluent reuse limits causing discharge issues during peak tourist seasons.
Extended multi-year CTO validities (5 years for Red/Orange, 10 years for Green) were implemented to reduce annual renewal frequency.

Technology upgrades are mandated for operation, including Zig-Zag systems with Induced Draft fans in brick kilns, fixed hood suction systems in induction furnaces, and continuous rotary furnaces in lead recycling.
Real-time continuous monitoring (OCMS) is being integrated directly into central and state pollution servers.
Continuous operational technologies, such as continuous rotary furnaces and fixed suction hoods, are adopted to minimize fugitive emissions.

Environmental Compensation under the Water Act (1974), Air Act (1981), and Environment (Protection) Act (1986) is strictly followed on industries under the 'Polluter Pays Principle' for non-compliance or environmental damage.
Officials suggest formulating region-tailored effluent management policies for hilly areas where standard treated-water recycling templates are unviable.
Officials suggest shared or subsidized monitoring frameworks for small units to offset the high capital cost of RTMS systems.
Officials suggest streamlining post-approval reporting workflows on single-window portals to reduce consultant dependency for small operators.

Common scrutiny rejections include non-compliance with prior CTE/CTO order conditions, failure to prove structural/technical adequacy of ETP/STP/scrubbers, and discharge parameters (BOD, COD, emissions) failing prescribed limits during inspection.
Field officers handle 2 to 3 districts per regional office.
CTO inspections verify output discharge parameter compliance (BOD, COD, stack emissions) and equipment adequacy rather than just the physical structure.
Processing timelines vary substantially by risk category - 30 days (Green), 60 days (Orange), 90 days (Red) - with a 3-day initial scrutiny SOP at the Regional Office.

gaps.text: The document header states 'Service(s) Discussed: Consent to Establish', but the entire content describes the Consent to Operate (CTO/CCA) process - likely a copy-paste error from the companion CTE document (identical date, location and experts).

The 'Documentation Required' list (architectural drawings, Appendix 7/8/9/10 completion certificates, power/water connection fee receipts, building photos) matches a building-completion/occupancy-certificate type filing rather than a pollution Consent to Operate filing - no ETP/STP, effluent, or hazardous-waste documentation is listed, suggesting the wrong checklist was pasted into this ED record.
The narrative process-flow step numbering skips from 'Step 7' to 'Step 9' with no Step 8, suggesting a step may be missing from the original ED notes.
The 'Statutory Fee' entry gives only the Rs 10,000 baseline figure; no fee slab table or multiplier showing how investment size or risk category changes the final fee is specified.

Mandated technology upgrades (Zig-Zag ID fans for brick kilns, fixed hood suction for induction furnaces, continuous rotary furnaces for lead recycling) are described as concrete operational reforms to reduce fugitive emissions.

Multi-year CTO validity (10 years Green, 5 years Orange/Red) is cited as reducing annual renewal frequency, but no quantified before/after figure (unlike the CTE record's ~8,000/year statistic) is given for CTO specifically.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Uttarakhand Fire & Emergency Services - District Chief Fire Officer (CFO) for low/medium-hazard cases; Headquarters Joint Committee (Deputy Director Technical as Nodal Officer, FSO HQ) with issuance by CFO after HQ pre-approval for large/high-hazard cases

portal.name: Departmental Fire Portal (ukfireservices.com) and the State Single Window Portal - a dual-intake system

timeline.basis: Two-stage statutory timeline stated in the ED's 'Application Timeline' entry: Map/CTE Approval Stage is a fixed 15-day processing window; the Pre-Operational (CTO) Stage, including physical inspection, is processed within 30 days.
timeline.text: The Map Approval stage has a fixed 15-day processing window, and the subsequent Pre-Operational stage (including physical inspection) is processed within 30 days.

documents: CTE/Map Approval Stage: Authorization letter from the competent authority (or reference letter / possession letter / objection letter)
CTE/Map Approval Stage: Structural Maps - Site Plan, Key Plan, Floor Plan, Elevation Plan, Section Plan, Area Statement, and Terrace Plan as per Uttarakhand Bylaws and NBC
CTE/Map Approval Stage: Fire Layout Plan detailing fire water tanks, pump house diagrams, emergency exits, entry points, travel distances, and building height
CTE/Map Approval Stage: Modified/Updated Compounding ('Saman') Maps, if compounding, alteration, or additional construction is involved
CTE/Map Approval Stage: Copy of previously issued Fire NOC (if issued previously)

Pre-Operational/CTO Stage: Approved Building Map duly approved by competent authority (SIDA/MDDA/HRDA/DDA/Jila Panchayat/Regulated area development authority/CEO cantonment board) demonstrating implemented fire safety measures
Pre-Operational/CTO Stage: Applicant Declaration & Equipment List - self-certified list of existing fire safety equipment per NBC and working condition status
Pre-Operational/CTO Stage: Equipment BIS/OEM Proof - purchase documents showing valid BIS approvals (e.g., IS 15683, IS 2190) from OEM, and PESO/CCOE certifications where applicable
Pre-Operational/CTO Stage: Copy of previously issued Fire NOC (if issued previously)

deemedApproval.text: Provision for deemed approval currently exists across all risk-based categories. A concern has been raised to withdraw deemed approval for medium- and high-risk industries, but this is still under discussion and has not been implemented.

validity.text: 5 years for residential buildings (excluding hotels); 3 years for commercial and industrial establishments (commercial buildings, hotels, industrial establishments, educational institutions, shopping complexes, hospitals, warehouses, petroleum/explosive storage facilities), with mandatory 6-monthly self-audit filings in between.

fees.text: No government fee applied under current rules.

steps.title: Submit application via departmental or Single Window portal
steps.note: Applicants may submit via the departmental portal (ukfireservices.com) or the State Single Window Portal.

steps.title: Submit application with structural and fire layout plans
steps.note: For new constructions, this is initiated during the building map approval/construction stage.

steps.title: Route to Development Authority and Fire Department
steps.note: Application and building plans routed through the integrated system for scrutiny.

steps.title: Fire Department examines plans
steps.note: Checks layout, setbacks, emergency access roads and fire safety system designs against NBC Part-4 and Uttarakhand Building Bye-laws.

steps.title: Rectify deficiencies if plans incomplete/non-compliant
steps.note: Applicant must rectify and resubmit.

steps.title: Fire plan/map approval
steps.note: Allows the applicant to proceed with construction per approved plans.

steps.title: Install fire safety equipment post-construction
steps.note: Installed per the approved plan, NBC, and applicable building bye-laws.

steps.title: Submit Fire NOC application
steps.note: Includes a self-certified declaration, list of installed fire safety equipment, and relevant BIS/OEM supporting documents.

steps.title: Route by risk category
steps.note: Large/high-hazard applications go through the Headquarters Joint Committee; low- and medium-hazard applications are handled at district level.

steps.title: On-site inspection by FSO
steps.note: Verifies installed fire safety systems and equipment against the submitted declaration and applicable standards.

steps.title: Rectify deficiencies if identified during inspection
steps.note: Compliance may be re-verified after rectification.

steps.title: Approval and issuance of Fire NOC
steps.note: Issued by the competent authority/CFO upon satisfactory compliance and inspection.

steps.title: Maintain systems, self-audit, and renew
steps.note: Applicant must maintain fire safety systems, undertake periodic self-audits, and apply for renewal before expiry.

remarks: The Uttarakhand Fire and Emergency Services processes between 3,000 and 3,500 Fire NOC applications annually across all 13 districts.
Roughly 80% of applicants belong to micro or small enterprises.
Exemption from obtaining a Fire NOC does not exempt owners from complying with fire safety standards; the Fire Department retains statutory rights to inspect premises and issue rectification notices.

findings.text: Fire officers currently lack statutory powers to issue direct penalties or challans during field inspections.
Following up on delayed 6-monthly self-audits requires manual issuance of notices, as there is no automated tracking.

An upcoming Uttarakhand Fire Service Act Revision Bill (aligned with Model Building Bylaws 2019) would empower officers with direct penalty/challan authority, introduce revised statutory fee structures, establish mandatory enforcement and legal liabilities for delayed self-audits, and formally define appellate mechanisms.
A jointly finalized inter-departmental collaborative checklist allows all legal requirements to be satisfied in one single submission.
District CFOs mandatorily re-inspect at least 10% of field cases already checked by FSOs as a supervisory cross-verification accountability measure.
The June 2025 Government Order introduced low-rise building relaxations (height < 12m) to ease compliance.
Officials suggest integrating automated system-generated reminders for 6-monthly self-audit declarations on the Single Window portal.
Officials suggest fast-tracking the Uttarakhand Fire Service Bill to establish clear penalty structures and formal appellate mechanisms.
Officials suggest consolidating intake exclusively through the Single Window system to eliminate dual portal navigation.
Applications currently enter through two separate portals (the departmental ukfireservices.com portal and the State Single Window Portal), which officials recommend consolidating.

Applications are routed by risk category: large/high-hazard (height >= 15m or built-up area >= 5,000 sq. m) go to the Headquarters Joint Committee, while low/medium-hazard cases are handled at district level.
Residential buildings with height under 12 meters are exempt from the mandatory Fire NOC requirement, unless requested by development authorities.
Roughly 80% of applicants belong to micro or small enterprises.

Exemption from obtaining a Fire NOC does not exempt owners from fire safety compliance; the Fire Department retains statutory inspection and rectification-notice rights regardless of exemption status.
Objections frequently occur due to missing required documents from the published checklist, non-compliant fire plans, inadequate setbacks/open space for fire tenders, or inadequate access roads.
Deemed approval currently exists across all risk-based categories, though withdrawing it for medium- and high-risk industries is under discussion and not yet implemented.
No government fee currently applies to Fire NOC under current rules, but the upcoming Fire Service Bill proposes revised statutory fee structures for CTE and CTO applications.
The department processes between 3,000 and 3,500 Fire NOC applications annually across all 13 districts of Uttarakhand.
